headline: Al-Futtaim Contracting Launches FM and Fire & Life Safety Operations in Saudi Arabia
deck: The Dubai group is combining its facilities management arm with the fire and life safety division of Al-Futtaim Engineering to sell against the Kingdom's operating phase.
excerpt: Al-Futtaim Contracting has launched facilities management and fire and life safety operations in Saudi Arabia, announced at Big 5 Construct Saudi. The move brings together Al-Futtaim Facilities Management and the fire and life safety division of Al-Futtaim Engineering under a single Saudi offer.
content:
Al-Futtaim Contracting has launched facilities management and fire and life safety operations in Saudi Arabia, announcing the move at Big 5 Construct Saudi in Riyadh. The launch brings together Al-Futtaim Facilities Management, the group's dedicated facilities management division, and the fire and life safety division of Al-Futtaim Engineering, with the stated aim of covering the full lifecycle of a customer's assets rather than a single phase of it.

The facilities management side covers sustainable energy management, HVAC maintenance and property upkeep, aimed at commercial, industrial and residential portfolios. The fire and life safety division offers end-to-end fire protection across commercial, residential, industrial, retail, hospitality and infrastructure developments, spanning system design and engineering, equipment supply, system integration, testing, commissioning, operation and ongoing maintenance, delivered in line with Saudi regulations and relevant international standards.

The pairing is the interesting part. Fire and life safety and facilities management are usually procured separately — one during construction, one after handover — and the split is a common source of failure. Fire systems are designed and commissioned by one party, then maintained by another that did not install them, holds no design intent and inherits an as-built record of uncertain quality. Detection, suppression, alarm and life safety systems are also among the assets most likely to be inspected by an authority long after the installer has left. Combining them under one contractor removes a handover that has historically lost information.

The commercial logic behind the Saudi launch is the operating phase. The Kingdom has spent a decade awarding construction contracts at a pace it had not previously attempted, and the resulting assets are now arriving in service in volume. Every completion converts a one-off contract into a multi-decade requirement for maintenance, energy, compliance and eventual replacement. Estimates of the Saudi facilities management market vary widely by research house, but the range sits above $50 billion in 2026 with high single-digit annual growth, and the direction is not disputed.

The regulatory environment reinforces the fire and life safety side of the offer. The 2024 edition of the Saudi Building Code has been mandatory since 30 June 2025 and includes a dedicated fire protection module, and Saudi Civil Defence approval applies to occupied buildings. Maintaining life safety systems in a certified, documented condition is an operational obligation with an inspection attached, not a discretionary service line — which makes it one of the more defensible parts of a facilities management contract.

For Al-Futtaim, the move extends a diversified UAE group further into a market where international service providers have been expanding steadily. The competitive question in Saudi facilities management is no longer whether a provider can supply manpower. It is whether it can operate an asset: building management systems, condition monitoring, planned and predictive maintenance, energy performance and the reporting that owners increasingly demand. That is a capital and systems business rather than a labour one, and the providers repositioning towards it are doing so because the margin has moved.

The launch also lands in a market where the delivery programme has fixed deadlines and the operating obligations that follow them do not. Big 5 Construct Saudi runs at Riyadh Front until 2 September, with a co-located Saudi FM and Clean event covering facilities management and commercial cleaning, and it drew more than 1,000 exhibitors from over 50 countries under the patronage of the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources.
